third_over_first.note: The third storey diminishes further than the inherited Georgian attic-over-second ratio; the style's own diagnostic_tells name shortened third-storey windows directly.

height_proportion.rule_append: Second-floor storey height runs 0.80-0.90 of the first, and the third storey 0.60-0.75 of the first (hard constraint c04) -- a steeper, more visible graduation than the inherited Georgian rule. Equal storey heights read as twentieth-century Colonial Revival.
height_proportion.note: extends rather than specified: the inherited principle (each storey diminishes so the front sits down rather than floats) is still exactly Federal's own logic; only the numeric band tightens.

variants.note: Constraint c05: masonry is Flemish bond with joints no wider than 3/8 in and no quoins. Rusticated or heavily articulated masonry reads as Georgian or a later revival, not Federal.
Same prohibition as brick-quoins (constraint c05).

corner_quoin.rule_append: No quoins (constraint c05, soft): the corner is read in the flat wall plane itself, or by a flat applied pilaster, never by projecting masonry relief.

board_thickness_max_in.source: new-england-federal constraint c01, generalised to the style

corner_board.rule_append: Where a masonry corner is executed in applied board (flat fluted pilaster or a scored 'quoin'), the board does not exceed 1-1/4 in in thickness and the whole assembly is painted a single light colour -- exposed wood grain or a contrasting trim colour destroys the masonry illusion the style depends on.

cornice_projection_ratio_max.note: 1/25 of facade height, a hard ceiling; the inherited Georgian corona-at-full-projection reading is capped rather than replaced.

cornice.rule_append: Projection is capped at 1/25 of facade height (hard constraint c02): the cornice casts a shadow of an inch or two at noon, never the deep corona shadow of the Georgian original it thins.

frieze.rule_append: Frieze depth does not exceed 14 in (constraint c02); on the flat Federal wall the frieze is the field for applied composition ornament -- swags, urns, paterae -- rather than for carved relief.

variants.note: Not in the inherited Georgian list at all. Federal's second characteristic sash count alongside 6/6, both carrying the thinner Federal muntin.

muntin_width.note: Replaces the inherited single 0.875 in value with the style's own hard ceiling and typical range; muntins at Georgian width (1-1/4 in and up) collapse the style at any distance beyond fifty feet.

variants.note: Promoted from a Mid-Atlantic regional canonical to canonical across the style, and specifically centred over the entrance rather than merely in a centre bay -- defining_characteristics names the stacked fanlight-and-Palladian-window composition directly.

special_window.note: A New England Federal signature above all (see new-england-federal), but the style file itself names it as a defining characteristic with no regional restriction, so the promotion is made at this level.

variants.note: Elliptical, set flush in the wall plane rather than in a projecting frontispiece -- the single defining move of the style.
Blocked and rusticated jambs are a projecting, relief-carved Georgian device; Federal ornament recedes into the wall plane rather than advancing from it.
A projecting pedimented frontispiece is exactly the Georgian object-in-front-of-the-wall the style's own distinguished_from clause names against it.
Baroque furniture logic; Federal ornament recedes into the wall rather than piling up projecting scrollwork over the door.
Same objection as broken-scroll-pediment: a solid projecting pediment element the flat Federal surround does not carry.
Even at its thinnest the entrance carries the fanlight and sidelight assembly; it is never a bare opening.

max_projection_in.note: The door surround is the one element permitted to project beyond the style's general 3 in ceiling, and even it is capped at 6 in.

door_surround.rule: The entrance is a hole in the wall crowned by an elliptical fanlight rather than an object standing in front of the wall: no projecting frontispiece, no blocked-and-rusticated Gibbs jambs, no broken or scrolled pediment. Ornament is confined within 6 in of the wall plane (constraint c02).

variants.note: The style's single most recognisable feature: an ellipse rather than a semicircle, and set flush rather than in a projecting hood.
Required whenever a fanlight is used (constraint c03): an elliptical fanlight requires flanking sidelights and a single-storey entrance treatment.
Reads as Georgian, or later as the Greek Revival rectangular-transom marker (constraint c04 there); Federal's transom is always curved.
The plainest houses forgo the fanlight, but it is the style's own signature and its absence is the exception here, not the rule it is on the Georgian parent.

transom_sidelight.rule: An elliptical fanlight with flanking sidelights, spun in lead cames as thin as the craft allows; the entrance treatment above it is always single-storey (constraint c03) -- a two-storey portico over a fanlight converts the building to Greek Revival or Neoclassical Revival regardless of the trim below it.

variants.note: The Adam-attenuated Ionic, run at 9-11 diameters rather than Georgian's 7-8.
Named alongside Ionic in the style's own typical_ratios as the two Adam-attenuated Federal orders.
Georgian's heavier order; Federal thins rather than replaces the order family, and Doric's proportions read too solid for the style's attenuated register.
Arrives with Benjamin's 1830 Grecian plates, forty-plus years after Federal's floruit ends.
Same anachronism as doric-greek.
Federal's order is thinned but still drawn from a book to a rule (Benjamin's plates); an abstracted order with no measured authority behind it is a different, later habit.

authority.value: Asher Benjamin, The American Builder's Companion (1806), by way of Robert and James Adam's Works in Architecture (1773-78)

order.rule: One Adam-attenuated order -- Ionic or Corinthian, run at 9 to 11 diameters against Georgian's 7 to 8 -- governs the whole building; delicacy is a proportional decision, not a decorative one, and Roman Doric or any Greek order is out of register or out of period.

variants.note: Federal columns and colonnettes are more often plain-shafted than fluted; entrance colonnettes in particular are frequently slim turned or built-up shafts rather than a full fluted order.
Georgian's own plain column choice; solid at 7-8 diameters, against Federal's slenderer 9-11.
Reads as structural mass, the opposite of the attenuated colonnette Federal reaches for at the entrance.

entrance_colonnette_diameter_max_in.source: new-england-federal constraint c05, generalised to the style

column.rule: The column is drawn slenderer than any antique authority permits -- 9 to 11 diameters -- and at the entrance is very often reduced further to a colonnette that frames the door rather than carries a roof.

total_height_ratio_of_storey_max.source: federal-style proportional_system: 'entablature depth under 1/8 of the storey it crowns'

entablature.rule: The entablature is thinned along with the column below it -- under one eighth of the storey height it crowns -- so that the whole apparatus reads as a band rather than a projecting order.

reeded_or_flat.value: flat or shallow-reeded, applied in low relief

pilaster.rule: A pilaster is a flat or shallow-reeded band applied to the wall plane, projecting no more than 3 in (constraint c02) -- the Georgian pilaster's engaged-column depth is exactly what Federal removes.

variants.note: Promoted over the Georgian modillion block, consistent with the style's own hard cornice-projection ceiling; a full modillion course cannot be built within a cornice capped at 1/25 of facade height.
Survives only at the largest scale of Federal work, and even there it is shallow relief rather than the deep Georgian block.
Applied low-relief composition ornament, frequently cast rather than carved -- defining_characteristics names it directly.
Doric, and later the Greek Revival marker Federal ornament is defined against.
Deep, bold Georgian and Corinthian carving; Federal's Corinthian, where used, is drawn as thin as its Ionic.
Bold Georgian relief; see modillion_dentil, where Federal specifies a plain bed mould instead.

relief.value: low relief, under 2 in, frequently applied composition (Coade stone or Wellford-type cast ornament) rather than carved in situ

concentration.value: frieze band, door surround, fireplace surround; never the corner or the plain wall field

ornament_vocabulary.rule: Ornament recedes into the wall plane: swags, urns, paterae, husk chains and reeding, applied in low relief -- frequently as cast composition rather than carved wood -- and confined to the frieze, the door surround and the mantel. The bold Georgian vocabulary of dentils, modillions and deep acanthus carving is exactly what is withdrawn.

variants.note: A small semicircular or elliptical portico on slender colonnettes, sized to frame the fanlight rather than to shelter anyone -- new-england-federal's own description calls it 'a frame, not a roof'.
A full-height, full-width colonnade reads as Greek Revival or Jeffersonian, not Federal; constraint c03 forbids a two-storey portico outright.
Two full storeys of superimposed order is exactly the two-storey portico constraint c03 forbids.

Federal thins the Georgian family rather than mixing in a new one; but the two profile sets are not interchangeable at the wall -- the Georgian pedestal and full entablature are heavier than the style's own hard ceilings permit.

trim_family.rule_append: The interest is reeded into the face of the moulding rather than standing proud of it -- Federal is not Georgian made smaller, it is Georgian made flatter, with composition ornament standing in for carved wood.

height_in.note: Overrides the inherited Georgian 8.5 in figure: 6 1/8 in in three members against Georgian's 6 7/8 in.

width_in.note: Overrides the inherited 6 in Georgian figure: 4 1/2 in in seven members.
